### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **55** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**59** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e24136c2f5af950db1c0ad977671e6804e6d769d`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 39 pages)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **56** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e24136c2f5af950db1c0ad977671e6804e6d769d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f770ea177fbbe86fe370fdc1176e111cb61f84a0` — the merge of head `d5c26da7a795e4fe9afc7e6115dbbe4299e2f89d` into base `e24136c2f5af950db1c0ad977671e6804e6d769d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f770ea177fbbe86fe370fdc1176e111cb61f84a0 && git checkout f770ea177fbbe86fe370fdc1176e111cb61f84a0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e24136c2f5af950db1c0ad977671e6804e6d769d d5c26da7a795e4fe9afc7e6115dbbe4299e2f89d && git checkout -B drift-repro e24136c2f5af950db1c0ad977671e6804e6d769d && git merge --no-ff d5c26da7a795e4fe9afc7e6115dbbe4299e2f89d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e24136c2f5af950db1c0ad977671e6804e6d769d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e24136c2f5af950db1c0ad977671e6804e6d769d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line review of #31974 (B #31698 PR-1, `Part of`) at head bf86d963: CHANGES, one required fix (a stale bound column).**

**What passes**
- **Readers.** The R1/R3 readers read `permission_set_package`. A bound column is the exact `(package, name)`, through E3's catalog, with a new exact arm. A null column keeps D3: R1 is asked with no caller package, R3 with the row's `package_id` (`storedPermissionSetScope`). With two or more holders it refuses, naming every candidate and the `bind` command, and grants nothing. It never falls back to the first.
- **Writers.** The two write seams stamp by S2's rule. The install door, the cold-boot check and spec are untouched, so phase 1 still holds and nothing narrows. The no-clash CONTROL is byte-identical.
- **Overlays.** I checked whether an environment overlay of a package's permission set could be bypassed by the exact read. It can't. An environment item under a package-held permission-set name refuses the boot (`environmentHeldSecurityCatalogConflicts`), so the exact arm never skips a customization.
- **Admin standing.** `ADMIN_STANDING_SURFACE` and `GRANT_STANDING_KEYS` register the column. That's right, because the column now decides `admin_full_access`'s body.

**R1 (required): a bound column whose package no longer holds the name must not silently drop the grant.**
`exact → getPackageScopedItem(...) → not-found` makes a grant whose set *moved* grant nothing. For example, an upgrade of P moves `sales_rep` into its dependency D, or P renames and D takes the name.
- On main the bare name still has one holder (phase 1), so the grant follows the set.
- With this PR the column still says P (a bound row is never moved), and the user silently loses access.
- That changes an intermediate `main`'s answer under phase 1. Red line 3, reading (c), says every intermediate main behaves as today.

Fix, by the precedent of E1 Q3 (a stale ledger row keeps acting on the current holder and warns):
- If the bound package holds no servable item of the name, read the row as if its column were null. That is the D3 answer (no caller for R1, the row's `package_id` for R3): one holder grants, two or more refuse with the candidates, none is not-found.
- Warn once per `(row package, name)`, naming the stale package and what D3 answered.
- This is not a substitute pick: D3 answers only when it is unique, and refuses otherwise.
- Pins:
  - A set moved from P to D keeps granting, with the warning. Run it with the fallback ablated (red), then restored (green).
  - With P and an unrelated U both holding after narrowing (the test double), the stale row is refused, naming both.
- S4's report should list stale bound rows, so the operator can see them. That can be a one-line follow-up on #31971 if it doesn't fit here.

**Recorded for #31971:** the downstream bare-name readers listed in this PR's Acceptance notes are exactly #31971's scope. Its body already names them: the evaluator, `ExecutionContext.permissions`, `readDisabledCatalogNames`, the accepted `everyone` set, `cleanup-package-permissions`, the plugin-auth last-admin enumeration, `role-change-granted-set` and `catalog-set-in-effect`.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line re-review of #31974 (B #31698 PR-1) at head 4d46f6ad: PASS. R1 is cleared.** It lands once CI is green and the seat ACCEPTs.

**The stale-column fix.**
- When the bound package serves no item of the name, the exact arm strips `packageId` and asks the same `resolvePermissionScoped` with the rest of the scope. R1 is asked with no caller. R3 uses the row's `package_id`.
- The outcome follows D3: one holder confers the set, two or more are refused with the candidates, and none at all reads as not-found.
- Nothing is picked: the read takes D3's answer, or that answer refuses.
- It warns once per (stale package, name), naming D3's answer and the `os migrate stored-references` review path.
- Pins:
  - A moved set still confers, byte-identical to an unbound grant.
  - A stale column with two holders confers nothing.
  - An R3 stale row reads from the suggesting package.
  - Ablating the fallback turns all three red.

**Seat 3's write pin.** A tenant or delegated-admin write of only `permission_set_package` leaves the column unchanged: by default the readonly strip drops it, and under `strictReadonlyWrites` it is refused. A system update writes it. Ablating readonly turns 4 pins red. The REST door does not set strict today, so the user sees a WARN and not a 400. That is still red-line-safe, because the column holds.

**Red lines 1–3 hold.** Under phase 1 every answer is as on main, with or without the column.

**Owed and recorded:**
- On #31971: stale rows in the S4 report, and every grant gate comparing (package, name).
- PR-2 (`Fixes #31698`) narrows after #31971 closes. It carries the B-card stances, seat 3's platform-`sys` stance, and `BUILT_IN_BARE_NAMES` for the platform-requested sets.
